title: Capitalize, title-case, and swap case
description: Write a function `format_variants(text)` that returns a tuple `(capitalized, titled, swapped)`: `text.capitalize()`, `text.title()`, and `text.swapcase()`.
examples:
format_variants('Coding For All')
-> ('Coding for all', 'Coding For All', 'cODING fOR aLL')
hints: Methods to consider: str.capitalize(), str.title(), str.swapcase()
.capitalize() uppercases only the first character of the whole string, .title() uppercases the first character of every word, and .swapcase() flips upper to lower and lower to upper everywhere.
Call all three methods on text and return them as a 3-item tuple, in that order.

hidden_tests.expected: ('Coding for all', 'Coding For All', 'cODING fOR aLL')
hidden_tests.label: source item 8

solution:
def format_variants(text):
    return text.capitalize(), text.title(), text.swapcase()
explanation: Each method targets a different notion of "case": capitalize() cares about the whole string, title() about word boundaries, and swapcase() inverts every letter independently of position.
